content:
alex_w: heads-up — CI flagged a quality regression after merging int8 calibration changes. invoice-parser eval shows structured JSON outputs failing schema checks, and hallucination rate jumped.

ci-bot: perf/eval run 2026-03-10T09:12:08Z job=infra-int8-calib #142 status=FAILED
ci-bot: metrics: structured_schema_fail=27%, hallucination_incident_rate=+9.2%, avg_latency_token=6.8ms (+1.1ms vs baseline), p95_lat=54ms

olivia_ml: thanks. repro on my laptop with the same quantized weights — I see JSON truncation and sometimes keys replaced with nonsense tokens at longer sequences.

ben_perf: can you paste the runtime kernel selection log? I'm wondering if we accidentally picked an aggressive packed-int8 kernel for some attention patterns.

olivia_ml: pasted below — note the kernel chosen for some layers:
```
2026-03-10T08:58:02Z runtime: model=invoice-parser-v3 quant=INT8 calib=per-channel
2026-03-10T08:58:02Z runtime: layer[3] select_kernel=quant_attn_fast_int8_v2 seq_len=512 head=32
2026-03-10T08:58:02Z runtime: layer[7] select_kernel=quant_attn_fallback_fp16 seq_len=64 head=32
2026-03-10T08:58:02Z runtime: KV cache policy=packed_prefix_cache enabled=true
```

chia: interesting — mixed kernels across layers and fallback on some seq lengths. Could calibration have skewed the scale factors for specific layers so int8 math changes token distribution?

alex_w: also seeing that batching heuristics pack short+long sequences into the same batch aggressively. That can expose KV cache corner cases with packed_prefix_cache.

nora: I ran a small ablation: disable packed_prefix_cache + force fp16 kernels -> structured schema failures drop to 3%, hallucinations back to baseline, throughput drops ~8%.

ben_perf: thanks nora — that implicates interaction between packed KV cache + INT8 kernel behavior. Two hypotheses:
- quantization calibration produced biased zero-points for certain heads causing deterministic token mapping breakdown in packed mode
- the fast_int8_v2 kernel has a subtle precision bug on long seqs when KV elements are reused from packed prefixes

olivia_ml: I can repro a deterministic case: when prompt contains long numeric table then model emits malformed JSON (truncated values). Stack trace shows invalid token id sequence at decode step. Dump attached.

alex_w: action items:
1) revert packed_prefix_cache in the INT8 rollout (quick rollback flag)
2) add regression test: invoice-parser eval prompt set added to nightly INT8 calibration runs
3) perf team to run microbench to compare fast_int8_v2 vs fallback_fp16 on long-seq KV reuse patterns
4) ML to inspect calibration histograms per-head and try per-block re-calibration

chia: I can do microbench. Quick note on methodology: test patterns should include varied batch packing (short+long), and repeated KV reads (simulate chat turns). I'll run across the GPU matrix.

ben_perf: I'll instrument kernel to log intermediate accumulator ranges and check for saturations/clipping. If we see accumulator overflow/excessive clipping in fast_int8_v2 we'll blame kernel implementation.

infra-bot: rollback flag created: infra:rollout/quant-int8-packed-kv -> paused (owners: alex_w, ben_perf)

olivia_ml: for the calibration side I think per-channel per-head asymmetric quant may help. Current pipeline used symmetric quant with global scale for the layer. I'll try per-head scale and rerun eval.

nora: small note — observed a different failure class where structured fields reorder unpredictably. That makes me suspect nondeterministic memory reuse in the packed KV path. added valgrind-like memcheck to runtime debug build.

alex_w: good. let's converge on a short-term safety: disable packed_prefix_cache for all INT8 deployments, add canary where we test per-head recalib + fixed kernel patch. We should ship rollback within 24h.

olivia_ml: I'll push a candidate re-calibration tarball tonight and run overnight CI; will post results tomorrow AM.

ben_perf: started microbench run on dedicated-qa (gpus: A100x8). I'll attach profiler traces when done.

ci-bot: job/infra-int8-calib #143 queued (with packed_prefix_cache=off)

alex_w: thanks all — keep notes brief here. If someone finds a concrete reproduce script, drop it in this thread and i'll escalate to oncall for a hotfix PR.

nora: quick repro steps I used:
```
python tools/repro/quant_regress.py --model invoice-parser-v3 --calib int8 --prompt-file repro/prompt_table.json --pack=true --seed=42
# observe malformed JSON in out.json
```

chia: running that now on ampere-qa.

chia: update — reproduced, log shows kernel accumulator clipping on layer 3 when pack=true and seq_len>256. attaching brief snippet.

ben_perf: got the profiler. suspicious memory aliasing at cuda kernel launch for fast_int8_v2. I'll open a PR to insert bounds-checks and reduce aggressive shmem reuse.

alex_w: perfect. we'll follow two parallel paths: (A) revert packed_prefix_cache for INT8 and (B) harden kernel + try per-head recalib in canary. Thanks team :thumbsup:
